g_policy.reason: The banner is opt-in, the offer copy states the reward (30 minutes without sponsored stories), declining changes nothing, and the 'if the ad fails' field covers both no game ready and a failed play.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 30 minutes of ad-free reading (feature_time), which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an article-open counter reaching 3 and a return to the feed, which are app events and involve no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed, locked or capped; sponsored cards are only hidden temporarily as a reward and return afterward, and the feed and articles work as before.

g_brand_safety.reason: The banner is a card in app chrome on s01 Home, which is rated safe, and it is not inside a conversation or next to unsafe or unknown content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: As a product change, the ad-free window is something the player uses in the observed core flows f01 (read a story) and f02 (browse the feed), and it goes to the player, not to a third party.

c2_evidence.reason: 'what makes it work here' states that a full-screen video ad AOL shows after every third article, and no mechanic or element in the product model supports that. The model records only native Taboola cards, and the banner also depends on a claim about how the app's ads behave that is not supported.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: No paid plan was observed, the reward expires after 30 minutes, and it takes nothing from other users or creators.

c5_moment.reason: The banner appears when the reader returns to the feed after finishing a third article, which is a finished action on a persistent surface, and never appears in the middle of an article.

c6_fits_simula.reason: This is a play-to-earn playable, the reward is granted only once the play is confirmed ('Once the play is confirmed'), and the trigger is a detectable article-open counter.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the home feed s01, the Taboola native cards s01.e44, s06.e33 and s02.e13, and the feed-to-article loop, so it would not read the same in another app.

other_concern: Whether the app can suppress network-filled Taboola cards on demand was not observed, and the revenue trade-off is only a prediction. The reward is also worth little if the feed slot is often empty anyway.
